checkpoints.description: [2/4] Version drift is fixed and guarded: __version__ is 0.2.0 to match pyproject, the CLI test derives its expectation from __version__ instead of a stale literal, and a new test reads pyproject.toml and fails when the two disagree (it failed first with 0.2.0 vs 0.1.0); 264 tests green

[3/4] Docs: ADR-019 records pyproject as the declared version and the guard test; README notes the v14 increment at 264 tests; codebase map regenerated; aikit check pebble 4/4 gates green; checklists: passed
Task 'task-pebble-v14-version' completed successfully.

[1/3] Plan: bump the declared version to 0.3.0 under ADR-020, because thirteen language increments (ADR-010 to ADR-018) have landed since 0.2.0 and the number no longer describes the surface; ADR-019's guard forces __version__ to follow

impact_assessment.why: The package still declares 0.2.0 after ten shipped increments that added eleven builtins and a fuzz guard, so the version number understates what a user gets and cannot serve as a release marker.
impact_assessment.benefits: The declared version describes the surface users actually have, and the existing version-coherence test proves the bump reached both files.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: --version prints 0.3.0; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: the two version literals change together.
impact_assessment.mitigation: ADR-020 records why this bump and not a major one (no v1 contract broken, only additions); ADR-019's test is the guard; full aikit check pebble gate.
